instructions:
Set up your Neovim config in Lua: ~/.config/nvim/init.lua.

1. If you already have ~/.config/nvim/init.vim, back it up first:
     cp ~/.config/nvim/init.vim ~/.config/nvim/init.vim.bak
   No init.vim? Skip to step 2.
2. Create ~/.config/nvim/init.lua. If you had an init.vim, translate each `set` line to Lua:
     set number          ->  vim.opt.number = true
     set tabstop=4       ->  vim.opt.tabstop = 4
     set mouse=a         ->  vim.opt.mouse = 'a'
     set clipboard=unnamedplus -> vim.opt.clipboard = 'unnamedplus'
     set cc=80           ->  vim.opt.colorcolumn = '80'
   `syntax on` and `filetype plugin indent on` are Neovim defaults, so you can drop them.
   `set nocompatible` and `set ttyfast` do nothing in Neovim, so drop them too.
   Starting fresh? A small baseline (change the values to taste):
     vim.opt.number = true
     vim.opt.expandtab = true
     vim.opt.shiftwidth = 4
     vim.opt.tabstop = 4
     vim.opt.ignorecase = true
3. If you used plugins in init.vim (e.g. with vim-plug), leave them out for now:
   lesson 10.4 sets up a Lua plugin manager.
4. If you had an init.vim, move it away so the two configs don't conflict:
     mv ~/.config/nvim/init.vim ~/.config/nvim/init.vim.old   (you already have the .bak)
5. Restart nvim and check your options, e.g. :set number? tabstop? expandtab?

Tip: write init.lua *in nvim*. Use your week 1-9 skills, e.g. paste the old lines
and convert them with :s and macros. :help lua-guide-options is the reference.
